name: Danbury Makerspace
summary: A 501(c)(3) nonprofit makerspace and coworking facility next to the Danbury Library, with its own entrance and 24/7 member access — and a 25,000 sq ft second site in development at the former Crowne Plaza.
description: Grew out of Mad Hatter Hackers. Occupies its own space alongside the Danbury Library with independent 24/7 member access, and is building out a second, much larger site at the former Crowne Plaza.

address.notes: Connected to the Danbury Library building, but a separate facility with independent member access rather than library hours.

operations.hours_note: Free public open house every Thursday 7–10pm except holidays.

equipment.notes: Eleven filament printers including Lulzbot Mini and Taz, and three delta-style machines
Table saw, chop saw, router table, drill press

sources.note: Superseded Google Site, recovered 2026-08-28 from its still-live sites.google.com address. Street address, website and descriptive text are transcribed from it verbatim. The logo is the space's own mark, recovered from the same page.
'CT Makerspaces Map' My Map attached to the superseded site. Coordinates are the 'Danbury Hackerspace' pin, transcribed from its KML, not geocoded.

Own site: 158 Main Street, connected to the Danbury Library; free open house Thursdays 7–10pm; expanding into the former Crowne Plaza at Exit 2 as Bright Ravens Innovation Studios, a 25,000 sq ft facility.
Own site: $50/month or $500/year regular, $25/month student, with 24×7 access to the facility.

Own equipment page, transcribed: eleven FDM printers (Lulzbot Mini/Taz, three delta-style) plus SLA; Epilog Helix 50W CO2 laser; ShopBot CNC router; drill press, chop saw, table saw, router table. Their Bridgeport mill is listed as out of order, so no machine-shop capability is recorded. The page says it is 'by no means an exhaustive list'.

Regional steward (MakeHaven) reports the organisation is officially changing its name to Danbury Makerspace, and that it grew out of Mad Hatter Hackers. The display name follows the steward; legal_name keeps 'Danbury Hackerspace, Inc.' until the entity itself is renamed. Their site, domain and logo still say Hackerspace.
